related_questions.question: What are the 5 steps of virus replication?

text_blocks.snippet: The five steps of virus replication are: attachment, penetration, replication, assembly, and release. These steps describe how a virus infects a host cell, replicates its genetic material and proteins, and then releases new viral particles to infect more cells.
snippet_highlighted_words: attachment, penetration, replication, assembly, and release

list.title: 1. Attachment:
list.snippet: The virus attaches itself to the host cell by binding to specific receptors on the cell surface.

list.title: 2. Penetration:
list.snippet: The virus enters the host cell, either by direct entry of the viral genome or by being engulfed by the cell.

list.title: 3. Replication:
list.snippet: The virus takes over the host cell's machinery to replicate its own genetic material (DNA or RNA) and produce viral proteins.

list.title: 4. Assembly:
list.snippet: The newly synthesized viral components (genetic material and proteins) are assembled into new virus particles.

list.title: 5. Release:
list.snippet: The newly formed viruses are released from the host cell, either by causing the cell to lyse (burst open) or by budding off the cell membrane.
